comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Final experiment and OSS research evidence, 2026-08-24

REAL PINNED READ / CONCURRENT WRITE
- Captured A=86b18cb9defc0a12074bf4a68efb22b5efed2dff. A one-ticket view listed and fetched 10 blobs / 62,426 bytes, materialized to a temporary directory, and reduced uncached in 29.156 ms total. Its canonical reduced-state hash b9a5e0dcbf3956e757aedbac5689357a6d5efb6e74fb48d48f8b0c52b1ecfb22 exactly matched the live target state. event_files_override created no .cache.json.
- A normal rebar comment advanced the live tracker to B=6e7f6b5619da0a5ee19e35e8d4e3ee06ecd746fc. Git proved A is an ancestor of B. Re-reading the A manifest was byte-identical; the unique mutation marker was absent at A and present only in the new COMMENT blob at B. This proves stable pinned reads while the normal store continues mutating.
- Compared with the observed 135,334-234,615 ms full-store materialization phases, the 29.156 ms scoped path was about 4,642-8,047 times shorter in these samples. This comparison isolates mechanics, not an end-to-end completion forecast.

DISPOSABLE VALIDATION FIXTURE
- Exact read plus children-of-target predicate manifest: an unrelated ticket COMMENT stayed valid; a target COMMENT invalidated the exact read; a newly created child invalidated the predicate even though the child did not exist at A; an incomparable revision failed closed before diffing.
- A .bridge_state/bindings.json change invalidated the global-context dependency and changed REB-1 resolution from bbbb-bbbb-bbbb-4bbb to aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-4aaa. Query/global reads must therefore be explicit dependencies, not inferred only from ticket directories already visited.
- Alias LINK gotcha: full-store reduction resolved sibling-alias to bbbb-bbbb-bbbb-4bbb; isolated target-only reduction retained sibling-alias. A scoped view needs canonical references or equivalent resolver context.
- Self-write gotcha: adding reducer-ignored COMPLETION_VERDICT changed the target tree OID from 2721aeb373f1965f5a899794f45d614f383c45b3 to 86e8e61b1d6971be788eaee918a36fe7649fcec8. Raw reduced hashes also differed, but only because the derived updated_at field advances; hashes with that presentation field removed were identical at d80deffc55665c2bfd07af61bc5aed952077727364a415bf5eaf00f1a1473ce6. A raw target-tree dependency would make completion conflict with its own sidecar write. Validation must distinguish state-bearing inputs from operation-owned observability events, or validate before any sidecar write and carry the result atomically into mutation.

ACTIVE OSS PRIOR ART
- Git, about 62.8k stars and v2.55.0 in 2026: immutable commit/tree OID plus lazy batched object reads and atomic ref advance. https://git-scm.com/docs/git-cat-file#Documentation/git-cat-file.txt---batch-command and https://git-scm.com/docs/git-update-ref
- libgit2, about 10.6k stars and v1.9.7 in 2026: in-process path lookup in an immutable commit tree without checkout. https://libgit2.org/docs/reference/v1.9.7/tree/git_tree_entry_bypath.html
- SQLite, about 10.3k stars on the official mirror and 3.53.4 in 2026: a WAL reader pins an end mark while writers append; stale promotion fails. https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html#concurrency
- RocksDB, about 32.0k stars and v11.8.1 in 2026: sequence-number snapshots plus transaction conflict checks. https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/wiki/Snapshot and https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/wiki/Transactions
- PostgreSQL, about 21.9k stars on the official mirror and supported releases in 2026: MVCC snapshots plus serializable predicate dependency tracking for phantoms. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/mvcc-intro.html and https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
- etcd, about 52.2k stars and v3.7.1 in 2026: pin a cluster revision and make historical range reads while newer revisions proceed. https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/learning/api/#revisions
- FoundationDB, about 16.6k stars and 7.3.77 in 2026: one read version plus exact-key and range conflict sets validated at optimistic commit. https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/developer-guide.html#conflict-ranges
- Apache Iceberg, about 9.2k stars and 1.11.0 in 2026: immutable shared metadata, atomic current-pointer swap, and explicit assumption revalidation before retry. https://iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/reliability/
- LMDB provides the same copy-on-write read-transaction pattern without a data copy. Btrfs snapshots are a filesystem-specific counterexample and do not meet rebar portability needs.

RESEARCH CONCLUSION
The recurring design is: capture one immutable version ID, read objects lazily, record exact reads plus predicate/global reads, then validate against the live descendant under the mutation lock and abort or retry on conflict. For rebar this maps directly to tracker commit OID plus Git object reads plus a typed dependency manifest. Whole-store hardlink copies, whole-HEAD equality, target-tree-only equality, and filesystem snapshots are not supported by the evidence. Removing checkout cost also does not remove broad list_states/reduction cost; that must remain separately instrumented and optimized.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Follow-up concurrency and current-process scrutiny, 2026-08-25, source d49466b5e960b401f58449abbc718e2e7d3f1bed.

A. LOCK WIDTH
The practical first design keeps verification, receipt validation, graph work, signing, event construction, and staging outside the global ticket lock. Under the lock: assert tracker HEAD still equals the validated Tn, assert expected root status, promote one prepared bundle containing PASS sidecar plus STATUS plus completion SIGNATURE, make one local Git commit, release; push remains outside. If HEAD moved, release without writes, validate the delta, and retry. This follows FoundationDB conflict validation, Iceberg assumption revalidation, SQLite short single-writer transactions, and Git compare-and-swap ref updates. With the current authoritative working tree, one local commit is the lower bound and must be measured before setting a numeric SLO. A deeper object-database design could prebuild the commit and reduce the lock to update-ref old-to-new, but live worktree/index consistency makes that a separate architecture change.

B. HIERARCHY AND LINKS
A single-ticket receipt is insufficient. Required receipt kinds are exact ticket state; direct-children membership; transitive-descendant reachability; outbound and inbound relation membership by relation; relation reachability where used; negative existence/absence; and global resolver inputs such as .bridge_state/bindings.json. Validation compares A..Tn changed ticket directories and recomputes predicates against both endpoints, catching newly created or reparented children and newly added inbound links. This is the PostgreSQL predicate-lock and FoundationDB conflict-range equivalent. Current rebar is inconsistent: structural close checks direct open children; landing scope walks transitive descendants; child certification trusts direct-child certificates; later completion validity fingerprints only root description, file impact, and direct child IDs. It does not bind child status/material/signature or deps. A child reopen/certificate invalidation or link change can therefore escape later parent validity.

C. UNANTICIPATED TICKET READS
The view must be lazy, not a pre-extracted allowlist. Any show-ticket request resolves and loads from the pinned tickets OID, then appends the actual ticket/object and resolver inputs to the receipt. A missing ticket returns explicitly not-found-at-this-revision and records a negative read. If it appears later and the absence mattered, validation conflicts and restarts at a newer OID. Alias/Jira lookup needs a pinned namespace index keyed by tickets OID. An unsupported query must fail closed or restart with a modeled receipt type; it must never silently fall back to the live store. This mirrors etcd reads at a historical revision and RocksDB snapshot reads, with FoundationDB-style dynamic read tracking.

D. PARALLEL REVIEWS
Each run owns run_id plus code_oid plus tickets_oid plus receipt. Immutable Git objects are safely shared. Derived indexes/caches must be external to the immutable tree and keyed by tickets OID plus reducer/policy version; temporary names must include a UUID. At commit, the first review advances HEAD. A second sees the CAS mismatch: unrelated deltas are validated cheaply and retried; relevant hierarchy/link/ticket deltas restart verification. Same-ticket closure is idempotent only when the existing closure binds an equivalent receipt and attestation; otherwise it conflicts. One atomic bundle prevents a losing review from leaving a durable PASS sidecar. This matches Git update-ref, FoundationDB transaction conflict/retry, and Iceberg optimistic commit retry.

CURRENT REBAR GOTCHAS
- transition_close runs structural and completion checks outside the lock, writes COMPLETION_VERDICT before STATUS, commits STATUS under txn.transition_core, then appends SIGNATURE under another lock. A loser can leave a PASS sidecar; STATUS can land without a signature.
- The STATUS critical section rechecks root status and selected lifecycle/plan policy only. It does not validate open-child membership, descendants, AC/provenance, commit evidence, child certificates, epic bug predicates, or a tickets OID/read receipt.
- Agent file tools use pinned code and show_ticket uses pinned tickets, but gate context, deterministic child/bug checks, and prefetch still receive the live repo root. The signature later recomputes current ticket material. A PASS can combine pinned code, pinned agent tickets, live deterministic tickets/code prefetch, and later signing material.
- The cross-run PASS cache binds criterion text plus code blobs, not ticket comment evidence or child-certificate state. Its fixed per-criterion .tmp filename also permits parallel writers to collide despite the atomic-write claim.
- Ticket snapshot publication is atomic but lacks per-SHA single-flight, so concurrent reviews can redundantly build the same large tree. Snapshot GC has no reader lease; ordinary tool opens do not use open_in_snapshot. Graph cache writes target the supplied tracker root and must be redirected for an immutable view.
- ContextVars isolate asyncio tasks but raw threads require explicit context propagation.
- A local store lock does not solve concurrent writers from another clone. Distributed correctness needs a candidate commit pushed by ordinary fast-forward CAS and receipt revalidation after any rejected push, or a single authoritative writer service. No force push is required or appropriate.
- Moving event preparation outside the lock must preserve HLC ordering, parent STATUS linkage, authorship signing, store compatibility, and append-only reducer semantics.

No source, tests, docs, or guidance changed. Primary OSS references: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-update-ref ; https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html#concurrency ; https://apple.github.io/foundationdb/developer-guide.html#conflict-ranges ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html ; https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/wiki/Transactions ; https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/learning/api/#revisions ; https://iceberg.apache.org/docs/latest/reliability/.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Plan approved and implementation handoff recorded, 2026-08-25.

CREATED EVIDENCE-FIRST BUGS
- `shimmery-customary-dorking` / 831f-326d-be85-437a — `--ref`-targeted completion may mix pinned code with live-checkout inputs. The ticket requires a divergent A/B real-path experiment and classification of every code read before any fix; intentional live comparisons may reject/retry but verdict evidence must come from the supplied `--ref`. A falsifying experiment closes the bug without a refactor.
- `lineny-barathea-ladybug` / 7dea-2f00-db57-4a96 — parallel completion-cache writers may collide on the shared per-criterion `.tmp` path. The ticket requires barrier-controlled thread and cross-process experiments, including suppressed-exception/final-payload evidence, before any unique-temp-path change. A falsifying experiment closes the bug unchanged.
Both bugs are linked `discovered_from` this research ticket.

APPROVED IMPLEMENTATION STORY
- `sedate-villainous-teledu` / b03c-f8d4-ef82-4618 — use a lazy pinned ticket view and atomically publish completion-close artifacts. The story pins independent `code_oid` and `tickets_oid`, records typed exact/negative/hierarchy/link/global read receipts, validates relevant deltas, keeps expensive work outside the lock, and makes PASS `COMPLETION_VERDICT` + closing `STATUS` + completion `SIGNATURE` one rollback-safe local commit before ordinary fast-forward publication. It explicitly forbids force ref updates/pushes.
- Concrete file impact: 14 source/test/doc paths. Verification: focused lazy-view and atomic-close suites, compatibility suites, then lint/typecheck/test in CI. No local suite was run because the operator requested CI-only testing on this resource-limited host.
- Signed plan review: PASS, 0 blocking / 5 advisory, verified at code SHA 8b8fa7c0064557c6746afc948e3cb0a8786c83a1, material 131e841d6c8bd7cf, Bedrock Claude Sonnet 4.6. Total 216,867.7 ms (3m36.9s), deterministic 5,796.9 ms, LLM 188,974.7 ms, 29 model requests.
- Advisory implementation guardrails retained without invalidating the approved signed plan: assert bounded object reads/no full materialization; make individual AC oracles explicit; bound repeated push-CAS retries and surface termination; evict stale OID-keyed derived indexes; reclaim per-run temporaries on abort/restart/crash.

No production code, repository docs, tests, or agent guidance changed during this research/handoff.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Live completion runs directly attribute 135-235 seconds to full ticket-store materialization. The store has about 5,500 ticket directories and 132,000 tracked files, so donor hardlinks avoid blob duplication but still perform work proportional to the inode tree. We need evidence for a stable read-only completion environment that pins tracker state cheaply while close, sidecar, and signature mutations continue against the normal live store.

## Approach
Use the tracker commit OID as the immutable read identity, because Git already preserves an immutable tree and the current implementation already resolves that OID before creating a checkout. Prove the boundary with Git plumbing against the real tracker plus a standard-library disposable Git fixture. The experiments will read objects lazily or extract only the selected real ticket directory; no full-store copy or production implementation is needed. Canonical parity is a fixture-specific observation, not a claim that arbitrary isolated tickets can resolve alias-form links without namespace context; the experiment must record that resolver dependency as a design gotcha.

## Scope
- Read-only Git plumbing against the configured `.tickets-tracker` repository.
- A temporary standard-library experiment harness under `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`.
- Ticket comments containing timestamped measurements and conclusions.
- No repository source, test, guidance, or architecture-document edits.

## Testing / Verification
- Benchmark at least 30 invocations of `git rev-parse HEAD`, pinned `git ls-tree`, and batched `git cat-file` reads against the real tracker; record median, p90, and maximum wall time.
- Extract the selected real ticket directory from a captured commit and compare its canonical reduced-state hash with its live counterpart using `rebar.reducer.reduce_ticket`; separately test and record the alias-link case that requires sibling or pinned resolver context.
- In a disposable Git fixture, capture revision A, commit a live mutation producing revision B, and assert reads through A remain byte-identical while B exposes the mutation.
- In the fixture, run `git diff --name-only A..B` and semantic predicates for exact-ticket changes, new-child membership, unrelated changes, and non-ancestor history.
- Record command output, timestamps, environment facts, and cleanup outcome as ticket comments.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Revision-capture timing for at least 30 trials is recorded on this ticket; checked from the harness summary for `git rev-parse HEAD`.
- [x] Pinned Git-tree lookup timing is recorded on this ticket; checked from the harness summaries for `git ls-tree` and `git cat-file`.
- [x] The selected real ticket fixture reduces to the same canonical target-state hash as its captured live counterpart; checked by the harness equality assertion. This fixture-specific result does not claim arbitrary alias-linked tickets work without pinned resolver context, which is recorded separately as a gotcha.
- [x] Pinned reads stay byte-identical after a later live commit; checked by the disposable revision-A/revision-B assertion.
- [x] The live view exposes the later mutation; checked by the disposable revision-B assertion.
- [x] Scoped extraction time, file count, and bytes are recorded on this ticket; checked by the harness summary.
- [x] An exact ticket edit invalidates its recorded read dependency; checked by the validation harness exit status.
- [x] A newly matching child invalidates the recorded child-query dependency; checked by the validation harness exit status.
- [x] An unrelated ticket mutation leaves the relevant dependency set valid; checked by the validation harness exit status.
- [x] A non-ancestor live revision fails closed; checked by the validation harness exit status.
- [x] Primary-source OSS prior art and design gotchas are recorded on this ticket; checked by cited URLs in the research comment.
- [x] No repository files change; checked by `git status --short` in the dedicated worktree.
